haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed in time, the sweeper, running every minute, marks it EXPIRED and stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. Inventory reserves all lines in one transaction. If any line is short, it reserves nothing, returns the short items, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The idempotency key (order id) on the charge call. Retries reuse the same key, so the provider cannot double charge. Payment rows are also unique on order id.
haiku-low.q4: Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and requests a full refund from Payment. The refund key is tied to the order, so retries are safe.
haiku-low.q5: Only on OrderConfirmed, which removes the lines in the order snapshot. On every failure path the cart stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service orchestrates each step and sets order status. Its order record, including status, holds how far a checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment (POST /webhooks/provider). Payment then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined, which Order reacts to.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores each provider event id in webhook_events with a unique constraint. Repeats get a 200 and are ignored. Payment moves each payment to a final state only once.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the reservation, moving it to RELEASED so stock is back on sale. Triggered by the declined payment outcome.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's commit succeeds only while the reservation is still HELD. If expired or released it replies RESERVATION_LOST, so Order cancels and refunds. Late success always leads to a refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund row stays open and is retried with backoff using the same key. After max attempts an operator is alerted. Pending refunds are tracked in the Payment service's refund rows.
haiku-low.q12: Order publishing OrderConfirmed, after reaching CONFIRMED status. Cart service handles it by emptying the lines in the order snapshot.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed, the sweeper (runs every minute) changes it from HELD to EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (reserve, then charge). If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, returns the list of short items, order becomes CANCELLED_SHORT_STOCK, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The retry uses the same idempotency key (the order id), so the provider cannot double charge. The payment row is also unique on order id.
sonnet.q4: Inventory replies RESERVATION_LOST (nothing committed); Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, requests a full refund from Payment, and emails the customer that the order is cancelled, out of stock, refund issued.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed (removing the lines in the order snapshot). On every failure path the cart stays unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order service, the orchestrator, moves it along by calling Inventory and Payment and reacting to results. The record is the order status (PLACED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.) stored by Order.
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook (POST /webhooks/provider) to Payment, which records it, moves the payment to SUCCEEDED or DECLINED and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined; Order reacts to these payment events.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores each provider event id in webhook_events with a unique constraint; a repeat is acknowledged with 200 and ignored. Payment moves PENDING to a final state only once. Consumers must also handle repeats safely.
sonnet.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the reservation (RELEASED), putting stock back on sale. It is triggered by the PaymentDeclined outcome from the provider.
sonnet.q10: It does not decide; the commit is a conditional update that succeeds only if the reservation is still HELD. If expired or released, Inventory replies RESERVATION_LOST and Order cancels and refunds. Late success always leads to a refund, even if stock is free.
sonnet.q11: The refund row is marked FAILED and stays open; it is retried with backoff and the same key, and after max attempts an operator is alerted. It is never dropped. Tracked in Payment's refund row (stored before calling the provider as REQUESTED).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order, causes the Cart service to empty the cart, removing the lines in the order snapshot.
